title: Transport in cells
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.1.3-c02 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.1.3-c01 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.1.3-c06 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.1.3-c09 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: 4.1.3-q01, 4.1.3-q06, 4.1.3-q09, 4.1.3-q02, 4.1.3-q07, 4.1.3-q03, 4.1.3-q08, 4.1.3-q04, 4.1.3-q05.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Concentration gradient
items.clue: The difference in how much of a substance is present between two areas.

items.label: Diffusion
items.clue: The net movement of particles from a higher concentration to a lower one.

items.label: Exchange surface
items.clue: Specialised for moving materials into and out of an organism, like the lining of the lungs.

items.label: Osmosis
items.clue: Water moves from a dilute solution to a concentrated one through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.stem: In diffusion, the particles of a substance in solution show a net movement:

options.text: from a lower to a higher concentration, requiring energy
from a lower to a higher concentration, using no energy
from a higher to a lower concentration, without energy
from a higher to a lower concentration, requiring energy

questions.explanation: Diffusion is the spreading out of the particles of any substance in solution, or particles of a gas, resulting in a net movement from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration, and it does not require energy from respiration.

questions.stem: Osmosis takes place through a partially permeable membrane. Which statement describes it correctly?

options.text: Water moves from a concentrated solution to a dilute one
Water moves from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one
Sugar moves from a dilute solution to a concentrated one
Solutes move from a concentrated solution to a dilute one

questions.explanation: Osmosis is the diffusion of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.stem: Root hair cells take up mineral ions from a very dilute solution in the soil. How are the mineral ions taken up?

options.text: By active transport, which uses energy from respiration
By diffusion, moving down the concentration gradient
By osmosis, across the partially permeable membrane
By diffusion, moving up the concentration gradient

questions.explanation: Active transport moves substances from a more dilute solution to a more concentrated solution, against a concentration gradient, and requires energy from respiration. This allows mineral ions to be absorbed into plant root hairs from very dilute solutions in the soil.

questions.stem: The concentration of oxygen in the air inside the alveoli is raised. Everything else, including the temperature, stays the same. What happens to the rate of diffusion of oxygen into the blood?

options.text: It falls, as a steeper gradient crowds particles
It stays the same, as the temperature has not risen
It falls, as the particles collide with one another
It rises, as the concentration gradient is steeper

questions.explanation: The difference in concentrations (concentration gradient) is a factor which affects the rate of diffusion, so raising the oxygen concentration in the alveoli increases the rate at which oxygen diffuses into the blood.

questions.stem: A potato cylinder has a mass of 4.0 g at the start. After 30 minutes in a sugar solution its mass is 3.4 g. What is the percentage loss of mass, and how is it found?

options.text: 17.6%, dividing the change by the final mass
15.0%, dividing the change by the starting mass
85.0%, dividing the final mass by the start mass
117.6%, dividing start mass by the final mass

questions.explanation: The change in mass is 4.0 g minus 3.4 g, which is 0.6 g. Percentage loss of mass = (0.6 divided by 4.0) multiplied by 100 = 15.0%, using the starting mass of the plant tissue.

questions.stem: Cube A has sides 1 mm long. Cube B has sides 2 mm long. Which statement about their surface area to volume ratios is correct?

options.text: Cube A has a ratio of 3:1; cube B has a ratio of 6:1
Cube A has a ratio of 6:1; cube B has a ratio of 3:1
Cube A has a ratio of 3:1; cube B has a ratio of 12:1
Cube A has a ratio of 6:1; cube B has a ratio of 12:1

questions.explanation: Cube A: surface area 6 mm2, volume 1 mm3, ratio 6:1. Cube B: surface area 24 mm2, volume 8 mm3, ratio 3:1. The smaller cube has the relatively large surface area to volume ratio, as a single-celled organism does.

questions.stem: A student plots percentage change in mass of potato cylinders on the y-axis against concentration of sugar solution on the x-axis. The line crosses the x-axis, at zero percentage change in mass, at 0.30 mol/dm3. What does this point show?

options.text: Water moved into the cells from the sugar solution
Water moved out of the cells into the sugar solution
The sugar moved from the solution into the cells
The cells and the solution had equal concentrations

questions.explanation: At zero percentage change in mass there is no net movement of water by osmosis, so the cell contents and the external solution are at the same concentration, and 0.30 mol/dm3 is the concentration inside the potato cells.

questions.stem: Why do large multicellular organisms need specialised exchange surfaces and a transport system?

options.text: Their surface area to volume ratio is too small for diffusion
Their surface area to volume ratio is too high for diffusion
Their surface area to volume ratio increases as they get bigger
Their surface area to volume ratio grows with their surface area

questions.stem: Which feature of the alveoli in the lungs increases the effectiveness of gas exchange?

options.text: A thick wall holding the gases in for longer
A small surface area that packs the cells in
A thin wall giving a short diffusion path
A thick wall that slows the escape of gases

questions.explanation: The effectiveness of an exchange surface is increased by a membrane that is thin, to provide a short diffusion path, so oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse quickly between the alveoli and the blood.
